description.value:
Biochem engineers run their laboratory out of a backpack, mixing kolto compounds, acids, and toxins with the same care a surgeon gives a scalpel. Chemistry, to them, is just another kind of engineering — one measured in vials and dosages instead of bolts and circuits.

Whatever the moment calls for, their modified pack has an answer ready to spray: a burst that stings like acid, a draught that steadies a bleeding ally, or a mist that leaves an enemy gagging. Few engineers do more to keep a squad alive while quietly poisoning everyone shooting at it.
